Article Title: BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami interact with youth in Haldwani
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami and BJP national president Nitin Nabin interact with youth in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, on September 20, 2026.

Nabin cites central schemes, emerging opportunities

Dhami highlights recruitment, self-employment

Sports infrastructure, technology and investment

HALDWANI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani, where they discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of Uttarakhand with young participants.During the interaction, participants raised questions related to the development of the state and the country. They also shared their experiences of various government schemes and offered suggestions on employment, self-employment and access to better opportunities in Uttarakhand.Nabin said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the potential of India’s youth was being given a new direction while new opportunities were being created for them. He said initiatives such as Digital India, Startup India, Skill India, Make in India and Khelo India had provided young people with platforms to advance according to their talent, capabilities and skills. He added that young people were not merely seeking employment but were also emerging as creators of jobs and new opportunities.He said the role of youth was increasing amid a rapidly changing economy and advances in technology.According to him, new avenues had opened up in areas such as artificial intelligence, startups, innovation, digital technology and entrepreneurship. He said Uttarakhand’s young people had immense talent and potential and that connecting their energy and capabilities with the state’s development could help take Uttarakhand to new heights.He said that in a mountainous state such as Uttarakhand, it was important to expand opportunities in local employment, self-employment, tourism, skill development and entrepreneurship. He added that the ideas, suggestions and aspirations of young people could play an important role in determining the future direction of the state. He called on the youth to turn future challenges into opportunities and actively contribute to building a developed India.He also described social media as a powerful medium and said young people should use it positively for the development of society and the country. He said all 1.4 billion citizens would need to work together to realise the vision of a developed India. He also urged young people to enter politics and public life and contribute to nation-building. He stressed the importance of time management, saying effective use of time was essential for success.Dhami described young people as the country’s greatest strength and said India’s large youth population was providing the nation with new energy, fresh ideas and capabilities. He said the growing use of technology and innovation was also opening up new opportunities for young people.The chief minister said that after assuming office on July 4, 2021, his government began working with the resolve that “the youth and water of the mountains should both serve Uttarakhand.” He said recruitment to vacant posts in government departments was accelerated and that around 34,000 young people had so far been appointed to government services. He also referred to action against irregularities in recruitment examinations, saying members of cheating rackets had been sent to jail and that a crackdown had been launched against those attempting to jeopardize the future of young people.He said the government was not limiting opportunities to government jobs and was also focusing on self-employment, startups and entrepreneurship. He cited the Chief Minister’s Self-Employment Scheme, skill development programmes, homestays and the Chief Minister’s Udyaman Khiladi Scheme as initiatives through which young people were being provided opportunities.The chief minister said Uttarakhand was establishing a new identity in sports and that sports infrastructure was being expanded across the state. He referred to work towards setting up a Sports University in Haldwani and a women’s Sports College in Lohaghat. He also cited Uttarakhand athletes winning more than 100 medals at the National Games, describing it as evidence of the state’s growing sporting talent and changing sports environment.He said opportunities were being created for young people in tourism, local products, science, innovation, artificial intelligence, robotics and other emerging technologies. He also referred to the Investors Summit, saying it had been organized with the objective of generating new investment and employment opportunities, while efforts were under way to expand industrial activity in the mountainous regions of the state.The chief minister said the government was also providing free coaching facilities to young people preparing for competitive examinations to help ensure equal opportunities. He added that the talent, hard work and potential of Uttarakhand’s youth were among the state’s greatest strengths in its effort to build a developed Uttarakhand.BJP state president Mahendra Bhatt, MP Ajay Bhatt, public representatives, party office-bearers and a large number of young people were present at the programme.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand cm pushkar singh dhami and bjp national president nitin nabin interact with youth in haldwani, uttarakhand, on september 20, 2026. Nabin cites central schemes, emerging opportunities, and sports infrastructure, technology and investment.dhami highlights recruitment, self-employment and skill development.

Article Title: Need social media firewalls, safeguards for minors: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With minors' access to social media platforms banned in many countries, Supreme Court Thursday took the first step in this regard by seeking govt's response to a PIL that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract - which is impermissible for a person below 18 years of age under Indian law.The plea by senior advocate H S Phoolka, on behalf of NGO Just Rights for Children Association, found resonance with a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which said there was a need for safeguards and firewalls to protect minors.Phoolka said children were at present permitted to independently create and maintain accounts on social media platforms and access digital platforms "notwithstanding their statutory incapacity to enter into a contract under Section 11 of Indian Contract Act, 1872", and said such contracts are void ab initio.The NGO said the absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposed children to "foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content and other harms affecting their safety, dignity, development and well-being".It requested the court to direct govt to ensure that persons below 18 years of age are not permitted to enter into contracts with digital platforms, including social media, online gaming, content-sharing, live-streaming and other user generated content platforms. It said minors could be permitted to access lawful, educational and age-appropriate digital content through accounts maintained and controlled by their parents or guardians, subject to an appropriate regulatory framework.Phoolka said social media platforms applied US law in India, not Indian law. In US, a person above 13 years can lawfully enter into a contract. CJI Kant said, "We need some safeguards in India." Justice Bagchi said, "There should be some firewalls."The NGO said opening of accounts includes acceptance of contractual terms and conditions, user agreements, privacy policy, etc, which govern the relationship between the platform and the user.Referring to provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the NGO said Section 9 required verifiable parental or guardian consent for processing a child's personal data. The Act also imposes restrictions concerning detrimental processing, tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising, it said.However, the existing statutory framework does not expressly prohibit a person below 18 from independently creating an account on a digital platform nor does it prescribe a uniform mechanism for preventing such independent opening of accounts, it said.
Article Summary: Supreme court seeks govt's response to a pil that said opening a social media account is akin to signing a contract. The plea by senior advocate h s phoolka found resonance with a bench of cji surya kant and justices joymalya bagchi and v mohana.

Article Title: India's investment in innovation low, we need to develop our own engine for combat aircraft: Ex-DRDO head Saraswat
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former DRDO head and NITI Aayog member Vijay Kumar Saraswat said on Thursday that India’s investment in innovation and research is very low as compared to developed countries and the govt needed to invest more on that front.Speaking at AEDEX + AIRPORT Expo 2026 in Delhi, Saraswat, “We need to invest more in innovation and research, allow more transfer of technologies from DRDO to the Indian private sector for bulk production of critical weapons, key govt organisations should do hand-holding of the private sector, and govt defence organisations should open their facilities to private sector for testing their weapons for accelerating the production of critical systems and subsystems needed for developing combat aircraft like AMCA. ”India spends roughly 0.8% of its GDP on research and development, which falls short compared to major economies. Developed nations like the US, South Korea, and Israel allocate between 2.7% and 5% of their GDP toward R&D.Talking about the delay in delivery of Tejas Mk1A aircraft due to late supply of GE F404-IN20 engines from the American company GE, Saraswat said, “We should learn from GE F404 and make our own engine.”Amitabh Saraf, programme director (combat aircraft) and director of Aeronautical Development Agency, said, “ADA has developed a lot of indigenous systems. But developing a combat aircraft is a very complicated exercise. We still need a lot of indigenous systems and subsystems for the fighter project. We still need to import flight control, AC generators, hydraulic and fuel pumps, and carbon fibre.”

Article Title: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is still alive and helping in subsequent future lunar missions: Sr Indian scientist
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A senior Indian space scientist on Thursday said that the orbiter of the Chandrayaan-2 mission, which was said to be a failed mission after its lander crashlanded on the south pole region of Moon, is still alive and is helping in planning and executing subsequent Indian lunar missions.During the AEDEX conference at Yashobhoomi here on Thursday, Anil Bhardwaj, director of Ahmedabad-based Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) under the Department of Space, said, “It was the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter that provided crucial information to Isro about where to land the Chandrayaan-3 lander.”Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which was launched in 2019, is currently operating from the Moon’s orbit. “It has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the Moon. It is now being used for future missions,” Bhardwaj said.Chandrayaan-2 orbiter carried eight scientific payloads designed to study the lunar surface, minerals, and exosphere. The orbiter is equipped with the Orbiter High Resolution Camera (OHRC), which features a spatial resolution of about 0.25 meters (25 cm) to 0.32 meters per pixel from a 100-kilometer lunar orbit.“For Chandrayaan-4, we have built sensors that will help in landing and bringing back lunar samples back to Earth,” the PRL director said.“Chandrayaan-5 will be a joint mission with Japan agency JAXA, where the lander will try to land in the permanently-shadowed region of the Moon. This region is near the south pole of the Moon and it never sees the sunlight. This will be a very challenging mission. The rover will go inside the permanently-shadowed region and explore for the first time the area. There again we are trying to put up very unique sensors to provide us information about the distribution of water.So sensor development is happening at a speedy level.”“India is also working on hi-tech sensors for in-situ (natural place) experiments,” Bhardwaj said. He also said the work is on in developing a heating system so that the lander can survive freezing temperatures during the 14 Earth nights (one lunar night is equal to 14 Earth days).
Article Summary: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is currently operating from the moon’s orbit. “it has the highest resolution among all the assets in the world operating on the moon. It is now being used for future missions,” anil bhardwaj said.

Article Title: Space-based surveillance: Dhruva to get key systems worth €5m from Safran
Article Text:
French aerospace major Safran Space signed key contracts worth over €5 million with Indian space-tech startup Dhruva Space​​.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: French firm Safran Space, under contracts worth more than €5 million, will supply critical systems, including optical payloads, for satellites being built as part of India’s Space-Based Surveillance-3 (SBS-3) programme by Dhruva Space, a release from the French President’s Office has confirmed.The contracts, signed during the International Space Summit in Paris, cover communication systems, inertial navigation units, optical payloads and ground stations for the constellation, which is planned to be deployed between 2027 and 2030.SBS-3, a strategic project approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security, will comprise 52 satellites in low Earth and geostationary orbits and is aimed at providing the armed forces with persistent surveillance, secure communications and greater situational awareness across India’s land and maritime areas of interest.The programme marks an expansion of the private sector’s role in India’s strategic space capabilities. Of the 52 satellites, 31 are to be built by private industry, with the remaining 21 being built by Isro. The private-sector allocation has been divided among three companies: Antaris will build 15 satellites, while Pixxel and Dhruva Space will build eight each.Dhruva’s eight satellites therefore form part of the private-sector component of the larger SBS-3 constellation, rather than a separate constellation.The programme is expected to improve the frequency with which strategic areas can be observed and strengthen India’s ability to monitor developments along its borders and across the Indian Ocean Region.The Safran contracts will give Dhruva access to a range of French technologies for the satellites and associated ground infrastructure. Safran said the cooperation illustrates the rise of Indian New Space and the ability of French industry to support the development of India’s sovereign space capabilities. The company also said the partnership could open the way to further cooperation under future phases of the SBS programme.The Paris summit also produced two other India-related announcements. French launch-services provider RIDE! signed an agreement to launch two satellites for TakeMeToSpace, an Indian company developing orbital data centres. The deal builds on RIDE!’s collaboration with Indian space companies, including the launch of a European atmospheric re-entry capsule aboard Isro’s PSLV.Separately, French Earth-observation company U-Space and Indian company Axiscades signed a commercial cooperation agreement to explore the Indian microsatellite market, addressing both commercial and institutional demand.Together, the three announcements point to a widening India-France space relationship spanning strategic surveillance, satellite launches and commercial satellite manufacturing, with Indian private companies increasingly at the centre of the cooperation.
Article Summary: French aerospace major safran space signed key contracts worth over €5 million with indian space-tech startup dhruva space. The contracts cover communication systems, inertial navigation units, optical payloads and ground stations. Of the 52 satellites, 31 are to be built by private industry, with the remaining 21 being built by isro.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $300,000 cancer donation and $80 million orphanage claim sparked heavy controversy
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce donation rumor fails to hold up

Travis Kelce has previously warned about AI charity stories

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new viral story involving Travis Kelce has been exposed as false, after social media posts claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star and his fiancée had spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on a child battling brain cancer. The same posts also tied Kelce to an alleged $80 million orphanage project. However, no credible evidence supports either claim, with the story appearing to be another example of AI-generated celebrity misinformation.The claim began circulating on Facebook in late November, packaged as a dramatic breaking-news story about Kelce and his charitable efforts. Posts alleged that the NFL tight end and his fiancée had paid $300,000 toward medical treatment for a 2-year-old child with brain cancer.The story then went much further. It claimed the couple planned to spend $80 million building what was described as the largest free orphanage in the United States.For Kelce, the rumor is notable because it follows a growing pattern of fabricated stories that attach his name to emotional charity cases. The posts used images designed to make the claims look convincing, including pictures of Kelce and his fiancée alongside a hospitalized toddler and a building carrying a sign that read "Taylor Swift Orphanage."A closer look, however, found no credible news reports confirming the alleged $300,000 donation or the orphanage plan. The websites spreading the claim also appeared to be designed to attract clicks and advertising revenue.That matters because the story was not simply an unverified social media post. It was presented with the tone and appearance of a major charitable announcement, encouraging readers to accept an extraordinary claim before checking its source.The latest rumor also fits with an issue Kelce has addressed before. In April 2025, he responded on his "New Heights with Jason & Travis Kelce" podcast to another false claim about his charitable activities.While discussing the spread of fabricated stories, Kelce said, "This time I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or the outlets posting all this AI stuff."He also pointed audiences toward 87running.org, the website for his foundation, as a place to find authentic information about his charitable work.There is an important distinction behind the latest rumor. A real story reported in October 2025 said that his fiancée donated $100,000 to help the family of a 2-year-old child battling brain cancer. That genuine act may have provided the seed for the much larger fabricated claim involving Kelce, $300,000 and an $80 million orphanage.Kelce has also been involved in legitimate charitable work, making it easier for false stories to appear believable when they use his name. But the absence of reliable reporting is a major warning sign.The episode is another reminder that emotional celebrity stories can travel quickly online, especially when they involve children, illness and huge donations. For readers, checking the original source and looking for confirmation from established news organizations remains one of the simplest ways to separate genuine philanthropy from an AI-generated viral rumor.
Article Summary: Claim began circulating on facebook in late november, packaged as a dramatic breaking-news story. Posts alleged that the nfl tight end and his fiancée had paid $300,000 toward medical treatment for a 2-year-old child with brain cancer. The story then went much further.

Article Title: "I’m too scared": Angel Reese makes a bold promise about her love life and fans may have to wait for a ring
Article Text:
Angel Reese explains why her dating life stays private

Unapologetically Angel

Angel Reese makes one promise about her next relationship post

Unapologetically Angel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Angel Reese has drawn a firm line between her public career and her private life. The Chicago Sky star has made it clear that fans should not expect regular relationship updates from her social media accounts. Reese explained that the intense attention surrounding her dating life changed the way she views romance in the public eye, leading her to make one striking promise about what she will share next.Reese opened up about her approach to relationships during an episode of her podcastin 2024. At the time, she was speaking with stylist Law Roach when the conversation turned toward dating and the pressure that can come with being a highly visible athlete.The topic was especially relevant for Reese. At 6-foot-4, she is already one of the most recognizable players in the WNBA, and her life away from basketball often attracts almost as much attention as what happens on the court.She admitted that she was unsure whether she would date someone shorter than her, even though she did not completely rule it out.“I don’t know. I’m too scared,” Reese said when discussing the possibility.But her biggest message was not about height. It was about privacy.Reese had previously addressed the issue on social media after her dating life became a subject of intense online discussion. Her frustration was clear.“Now i see why people hide relationships & keep everything private 😭 like i don’t think i’ll ever openly share that part of my life with yall again until im married cause yall do THE MOST!”The post reflected a growing divide between what Reese was willing to share with fans and what she wanted to keep for herself. For someone whose professional life is constantly dissected, a private relationship offered a rare space where she could simply be Angel rather than an athlete under a microscope.Reese later made her position even clearer during another episode of, this time while speaking with Pretty Vee.“I think the next time I’ll post I’m in a relationship [on social media] is when I’m married,” Bayou Barbie said. “And that’s some time from now, so you ain’t gonna see it.”She followed that statement with another playful warning for anyone hoping to catch a glimpse of her dating life.“You might see me on a date. You gonna have to catch me though,” she continued. “Like, I’m not gonna post a man on my page.”A few days later, Reese reinforced the message herself.“The next time I’ll post in a relationship is when I’m married,” Reese wrote.Her stance makes sense in an era when a single photo can trigger days of speculation. For high-profile athletes, dating rumors can quickly become headlines, fan debates and social media arguments. Reese has experienced that attention firsthand, so choosing not to feed it gives her greater control over her personal life.Ironically, her relationship with Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. later became widely known despite her earlier promise. Rumors about the pair began circulating in early 2025, before Carter appeared at Reese’s birthday celebration and supported her courtside later that year.That does not necessarily erase the point Reese was making. Her comments were about refusing to turn a relationship into regular social media content.Reese's career has only made that boundary more important. As a first overall pick, three-time All-Star and one of the WNBA's most closely followed young stars, she knows almost every part of her life can become public conversation.Her solution is refreshingly direct. Fans can watch her compete, follow her career and celebrate her achievements. Her romantic life, however, does not have to become another performance.And if Reese stays true to the promise she made, the next relationship announcement may come with a very different title attached to it: husband.
Article Summary: Angel reese has drawn a firm line between her public career and her private life. The chicago sky star has made it clear that fans should not expect regular relationship updates from her social media accounts. Reese explained that the intense attention surrounding her dating life changed the way she views romance in the public eye.

Article Title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s fiancé Georgios Frangulis built his own empire before becoming her biggest supporter
Article Text:
Georgios Frangulis and Aryna Sabalenka (Getty Images)

Who is Georgios Frangulis, Aryna Sabalenka 's fiancé?

Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis (Getty Images)

How did Georgios Frangulis build Oakberry into a global brand?

When did Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis start dating?

How did Georgios Frangulis propose to Aryna Sabalenka?

What is 'The Gride,' Georgios Frangulis's new fashion brand?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores across 50 countries. Now 37, Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026, capping a relationship that began when she signed on as an Oakberry brand ambassador in early 2024.Born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil, Frangulis has Greek roots, with his family originally from Thessaloniki, Greece. He studied law at FAAP -- Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado -- in 2014, but never sat the bar exam."I always knew I wouldn't be a lawyer," he said. "What I really wanted was to be an entrepreneur."That clarity of purpose was rare at the time. Most people spend years hedging. Frangulis walked away from a law degree, moved to the United States, where he became infatuated with açaí, came back to São Paulo, and launched Oakberry in December 2016.Co-founded alongside Renato Haidar, Oakberry was not just another smoothie shop. Frangulis positioned açaí as functional nutrition -- clean ingredients, no artificial syrups, and a strong link to fitness culture -- and built a franchise model designed from day one to scale internationally.The company raised $67 million in capital in late 2023. By mid-2026, Oakberry had grown to a 900-location global business, with stores in Dubai malls, Miami gyms, Australian beach towns, and European city centres -- all without compromising brand consistency.In June 2023, Frangulis graced the cover of Forbes Brazil. The profile explored not just his entrepreneurial arc but his spirituality and Greek identity. His bicep tattoo reads "Fight for us, Saint George the Warrior." His forearm reads, "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." These are not the accessories of a brand persona.His net worth in 2026 is estimated between $75 million and $100 million -- built almost entirely from his equity in Oakberry, not from market listings or quick exits.They met in January 2024 when Sabalenka was hired as an ambassador for Oakberry. The couple were first spotted together in April 2024 -- a month after the tragic and untimely death of Sabalenka's ex-boyfriend, Konstantin Koltsov, who died by suicide in March 2024.It was a difficult period, and Sabalenka has been open about what Frangulis meant to her during it. "There was a really tough period where I was really happy to have him by my side, always cheering me up, always making sure that we are doing some fun stuff," she told People. "His support means so much to me. Being on the road and having him support me, to make me laugh and to be able to work out together, makes life on the road feel more like home. "Sabalenka had been broadly hinting for months. After winning the Brisbane International in January 2026, she said in her victory speech: "Thank you to my boyfriend... Hopefully soon I can call you something else, right? Let's just put some extra pressure."Frangulis proposed to Sabalenka in Indian Wells, California, on March 3, 2026. The setting was candlelit, with rose petals arranged beside a pool -- a rental home the couple had spent time in since the early days of their relationship. Sabalenka, in jeans and a white t-shirt, had no idea it was coming."I always knew I wanted to propose to Aryna because I was 100% sure she was the person I wanted to spend the rest of my life with," he shared in a YouTube video about the moment.The ring was designed by Isabela Grutman, who worked with Frangulis for months to create the custom piece. It features a 12-carat, oval-cut diamond surrounded by emeralds set in platinum -- Sabalenka's favorite stone, and also her birthstone. Experts told InStyle the ring could be worth up to $1 million. They captioned their joint Instagram post: "You & me, forever."Earlier in 2026, Frangulis launched his own fashion brand, named The Gride. The name honors his Greek heritage and mixes the words Greek and Pride. "My pride comes from my grandparents and has spread to my closest circle," the brand's website states. "The feeling is unmatched, and I'll do my best to make each and every one of you feel it too."Outside business, Frangulis races Porsche GT3 Cup cars. "Getting in the car and racing is one of the few moments when nothing else matters," he told Forbes Brazil. For someone whose professional life spans dozens of countries and time zones, that says something about how he recharges.What is clear is that Frangulis arrived in this relationship with his own story already written. He built a global company from a fruit most of the world had never heard of, then quietly showed up for the woman he loves at every stop on the tour. That is not a supporting role. It is just a different kind of ambition.
Article Summary: Georgios frangulis proposed to world no. 1 aryna sabalenka in march 2026. The brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores. Frangulis proposed to sabalenka in a candlelit setting at a rental home.

AHMEDABAD: The Daman administration on Wednesday made owners of Mahindra Thar and Toyota Fortuner SUVs take a road safety pledge.The initiative comes amid continued public debate online over the image of the two SUVs.“Thar and Fortuner owners participating in the ‘Thar-Fortuner Sankalp Yatra’ and taking the Road Safety Pledge administered by district collector,” the post said.A video shared with the post shows Fortuners and Thars lined up together as part of the rally. Article Title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max get Variable Aperture as 'most important' camera feature: What it means for users
Article Text:
Apple iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max

Aperture is the part of a camera most phone users never see

The useful bit is what happens when you take control

It is not just about low light

The aperture is only on one camera

Apple is adding more control to video too

The idea isn't new to smartphones

The bigger camera change is the combination

What variable aperture actually changes for iPhone users

Apple has added variable aperture to the main camera on both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. This will offer users a physical way to control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time on an iPhone.The feature sits alongside a new 48MP Fusion Main camera, a redesigned sensor and new Pro Controls. Apple says the six laser-cut blades inside the lens can move between four aperture settings, while the camera can also adjust the aperture automatically depending on the scene.That sounds like a minor hardware upgrade. But it is not. The lens opening affects exposure, depth of field, and how motion is captured, so giving the iPhone aperture control adds something software alone can't quite duplicate.Apple's description is straightforward: "iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48 megapixel fusion main camera with variable aperture for creative control that wasn't possible before," Apple said. "This is the most advanced camera we've ever made."Aperture is simply the opening through which light passes before reaching a camera's image sensor. It is measured using f-numbers such as f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0.The lower the f-number, the wider the opening and the more light reaches the sensor.A wider aperture can therefore help in darker conditions. A narrower aperture lets in less light, but it also keeps more of the scene in focus.Most smartphone cameras use a fixed aperture. The lens has one opening, and the phone relies heavily on shutter speed, ISO, and computational photography to handle different lighting conditions.The iPhone 18 Pro changes that for its main camera. Its lens can open as wide as f/1.48 and then stop down to f/1.8, f/2.8 or f/4.0. Six blades inside the lens physically change the opening size.Apple says the blades are laser-cut and thinner than a human hair. They are designed to move smoothly between the available settings rather than simply switching between two fixed positions.The camera can make that decision automatically. In a darker scene, it can open the aperture to f/1.48 and let in more light. In brighter conditions, it can narrow the opening.For most people, the automatic system will do most of the work. The Camera app can choose an aperture based on the scene, just as it already decides on exposure and other settings.The difference is that iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max owners can also take control themselves.Apple's new Pro Controls let users manually change aperture, shutter speed, and white balance. A histogram can also be displayed to help judge exposure across a scene.That gives photographers another way to decide how a picture should look, instead of leaving every exposure decision to the camera.The most obvious example is depth of field. At a wider aperture such as f/1.48, the camera can produce more optical background blur when the subject is relatively close and the background is farther away.Stopping down to f/4.0 has the opposite effect. More of the scene can stay in focus, which can help with landscapes or group photos where people stand at different distances from the camera.That matters because a group shot can otherwise leave one person sharp while another, standing slightly farther away, falls outside the plane of focus. A narrower aperture gives the camera more room to keep those subjects in focus.It also gives photographers another option when deliberately introducing motion into an image. A narrower aperture reduces the amount of light entering the lens, making it easier to use a slower shutter speed when conditions are bright enough.The obvious benefit of opening the aperture is light. Apple says the main camera can open to ƒ/1.48 for low-light photography, letting more light reach the sensor.That can give the camera more flexibility before it has to compensate by increasing ISO or slowing the shutter speed. In practical terms, that can help preserve detail and reduce noise, while a fast enough shutter can keep moving subjects sharp.But variable aperture is useful in the opposite direction too.In bright daylight, photographers sometimes want a slower shutter speed to create motion blur. That can be useful with moving water, people, or cars, and it also matters in video, where shutter speed is normally tied to frame rate.A fixed wide aperture can make that difficult in strong sunlight because too much light reaches the sensor even when the shutter is already operating at its fastest useful setting. Stopping the lens down gives the camera another way to reduce exposure.There are limits, though. A range ending at f/4.0 does not eliminate the need for neutral-density filters in every bright-light situation. Photographers who want long exposures in direct sunlight may still need an ND filter to cut the light further.Apple's implementation has an important limitation. The variable aperture is on the main 24mm camera. It does not extend across the entire rear camera system.The ultra-wide and telephoto cameras don't have the same variable-aperture mechanism. That means the new optical control is available only when shooting through the main lens.This is also why the feature should not be viewed as a replacement for the other cameras or for computational photography. Exposure, autofocus, HDR, noise reduction and image processing still determine much of the final photograph.The hardware simply gives the camera another physical variable to work with before those processes take over.Aperture changes also feed into Apple's video features. The new Pro Controls work with video as well as photography, letting users manually adjust settings including aperture and shutter speed. That is especially relevant for people who want more predictable exposure rather than letting the phone change settings during recording.Apple has also added the ability to apply Cinematic effects after capture to videos recorded at up to 60 frames per second. That means users can make this adjustment after recording instead of committing to the effect while shooting.Time-lapse recording now supports 4K and Dolby Vision HDR, while Audio Mix has new algorithms designed to improve voice quality and isolate music.The combination is notable because Apple isn't presenting the variable aperture as an isolated camera specification. It is part of a broader attempt to give users more control over how photos and video are captured and processed.Apple is not the first phone maker to put a variable aperture in a smartphone. Samsung introduced a dual-aperture system with the Galaxy S9 series in 2018. That system switched between f/1.5 and f/2.4 depending on the lighting conditions.Huawei later introduced more flexible variable-aperture systems, while Xiaomi and Honor have also used the technology in flagship phones.The reason it has remained relatively uncommon is fairly simple: fitting a mechanical aperture mechanism into a smartphone camera adds complexity to an already tightly packed module.For years, phone makers instead concentrated on larger sensors, multiple cameras and computational photography. Those technologies can compensate for many of the limitations of a fixed aperture without adding moving parts to the lens.The iPhone 18 Pro's approach is therefore less about replacing computational photography than adding an optical control alongside it.The variable aperture gets most of the attention, but Apple has made several other changes to the camera system.The 48MP Fusion Main camera uses a new sensor and a new computational imaging pipeline that Apple says produces sharper, more detailed images. Photographic Styles now include additional texture and grain controls, giving users more ways to change the look of their photos.Apple has also added persistent subject tracking for photos and video, letting the camera keep following a person even if they temporarily disappear behind someone else in a crowd.Another feature aimed at photographers is Apple Reference Image. When Reference mode is used, the camera captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute turns into what Apple describes as an "unalterable reference image." You can then view the reference alongside the main photograph in the Photos app.The idea is to compare the original sensor-derived reference with the photograph and identify whether changes have been made. Apple says the feature is intended to address image authenticity, particularly for photographers and photojournalists.Apple is also adding metadata support and upcoming support for the SynthID standard to help identify images generated or edited with AI.For someone who simply opens the Camera app and takes pictures, it may not change much. The phone can choose the aperture automatically, just as it already handles most exposure decisions. For people who shoot deliberately, the change is more useful.A wider f/1.48 setting can help in darker scenes. Stopping down can keep more of a group or landscape in focus. Manual aperture control can also be combined with shutter-speed control to create particular motion effects.It can even produce optical effects that fixed-aperture smartphone cameras cannot reproduce in the same way, including changes in how bright points of light appear at narrower apertures.But four aperture settings don't turn the iPhone into a dedicated interchangeable-lens camera. The sensor remains small compared with most conventional cameras, and the amount of natural optical background blur depends heavily on the distance between the camera, subject, and background.For many portraits, Apple's computational Portrait mode will still produce a stronger and more controllable background-blur effect.The same is true for long exposures in bright daylight. The f/1.48-to-f/4.0 range gives photographers more room, but it does not remove the physical limits imposed by available light.That is probably the right way to look at the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture. It gives the camera one more physical control over exposure and focus, while the sensor and software continue to determine what ultimately reaches the screen.For casual users, most of that will happen automatically. For photographers and videographers who want to decide how the shot is captured, the four aperture settings and Pro Controls make the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max considerably more flexible than a fixed-aperture iPhone.
Article Summary: Aperture is the opening through which light passes before reaching a camera's image sensor. Six blades inside the lens physically change the opening size. Apple says the blades are laser-cut and thinner than a human hair. They are designed to move smoothly between the available settings.

Article Title: ARC raises Rs 10.5 crore in pre-seed funding
Article Text: ARC, a gaming technology company has raised Rs 10.5 crore in pre‑seed funding led by Chimera VC and MIXI Global Investments, with participation from Dhruv Vohra, Director, Meta, APAC, in his personal capacity. The funding will accelerate development and commercialisation of ARC X1, covering hardware engineering, product validation, manufacturing readiness, and further development of OWL OS and ARC’s gaming software platform. It will also support team expansion, go‑to‑market capabilities, and strategic partnerships across gaming, cloud, content and technology.The global portable gaming console market was valued at US$3.89 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at 9.7% CAGR through 2033. ARC aims to tap into India’s large mobile‑first gaming community and the low penetration of dedicated gaming hardware, creating space for a more accessible portable gaming category.Founded by Jobin Joseph and Kaustubh K. Jadhav, ARC is building a platform that integrates hardware, software and gaming experiences. The ARC X1 is a portable gaming system designed to make dedicated gaming more accessible to Indian gamers.ARC is developing its own hardware and software stack, aiming to build an ecosystem across devices, operating systems, software services and gaming experiences.Joseph said the funding will deepen ARC’s technology, accelerate product development and move the company closer to launch. Jadhav added that ARC was founded on the belief that access should not determine how deeply someone experiences gaming, and the funding will help bring ARC X1 to gamers at scale.Chimera VC’s Krish Anurag said ARC fits their thesis of backing companies that can become infrastructure for the next chapter of gaming. MIXI Global Investments’ Tomoharu Urabe said ARC X1 can make handheld gaming more accessible for India’s passionate gaming community.ARC X1 is built on ARM architecture, powered by Qualcomm technology, and runs OWL OS, ARC’s proprietary gaming operating system. It supports native Android gaming, PC‑game compatibility through ARC’s software stack, and cloud gaming. ARC has crossed 50,000 waitlist sign‑ups and collaborated with Qualcomm ahead of launch, adopting a community‑led development model involving gamers through early testing and feedback programmes.
Article Summary: Arc, a gaming technology company has raised rs 10.5 crore in pre‑seed funding. The funding will accelerate development and commercialisation of arc x1. Arc aims to tap into india’s large mobile‑first gaming community and the low penetration of dedicated gaming hardware.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu warns companies against sharing sensitive data with AI labs: This is quite serious and …
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu raises AI data security concerns

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns about the growing use of frontier AI models by companies handling sensitive information. Quoting Fields Medalist Terence Tao, Sridhar Vembu shared an X (formerly Twitter) post that said companies with critical know-how, intellectual property and trade secrets should be careful about trusting their information with frontier AI labs. The mathematician warned that AI could change how researchers share ideas. Tao said, "The incentives may now be pointing in the direction of no longer sharing any promising research directions with the broader community, which would reverse centuries of traditions of open science and do serious long-term damage to the future of the field".Sridhar Vembu said companies with valuable intellectual property and trade secrets should be cautious about putting their information into frontier AI systems. "This is quite serious and it is not just mathematicians and scientists," Vembu wrote.He argued that the concern could apply to companies across industries that have sensitive information they do not want to expose outside their organisations.In the post, Vembu also highlighted the pharmaceutical industry as an example. He said major pharma companies already have their own AI models, often based on open-source models, to avoid giving large AI companies information about new drug molecules and processes they are developing."That caution is well warranted," Sridhar Vembu said.Zoho founder says companies should build their own AI models"Your company's know-how belongs in your own AI model," Vembu wrote. He also said that building and running private AI models is becoming easier and cheaper. “Fortunately they are easy to train and becoming cheaper to run too”.
Article Summary: Sridhar vembu raises ai data security concerns over frontier ai. He said companies with critical know-how, intellectual property and trade secrets should be careful about trusting their information with frontier ai labs. The mathematician warned that ai could change how researchers share ideas.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher who quit over AI safety walked away two months before his stock vested; says: I no longer have anything to gain by…
Article Text:
Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation.

Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch

Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

An Anthropic safety lead replied to the resignation thread and agreed with it

An Anthropic researcher who resigned this week over AI safety fears gave up his entire stake in the company to do it, walking out two months before his equity was due to vest.Jacob Coxon, 27, spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI before moving to Anthropic in July. He lasted four months. Staff need six for their stock to vest. His resignation post on X on September 9, now past 130 million views, said neither lab is acting responsibly and that both are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives".Axios first reported the forfeited equity, after Coxon told the outlet on Wednesday that "I no longer have anything to gain by juicing up Anthropic's valuation" and that he left before any of his shares vested. He still holds equity in OpenAI, where his work included GPT-4o.The company is preparing a listing at a reported $2 trillion valuation, built in large part on its reputation as the frontier lab that takes risk seriously. That is what gives the equity detail its weight. Researchers have walked out of rival labs over safety before, usually after their stock vested. Coxon left with nothing, then criticised the valuation he could have profited from.He drew that line carefully in the interview. Anthropic's safety work is sincere, he said, and he has not seen it compromised to outpace competitors. What worries him is pressure over time. Race hard enough and you cut corners, or skip steps in the oversight process. He also described a mood he thinks becomes self-fulfilling, calling it excessive paranoia about OpenAI and about China. Colleagues, he wrote earlier, have started using words like "crunchtime" and "endgame".His most quoted line was about where these decisions are being taken. It is insane, he said, that the work happens on the MacBooks of engineers in San Francisco rather than in a bunker in the desert like the Manhattan Project.Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress testing at Anthropic, wrote that he personally puts the odds of AI killing all humans above 10 percent within the decade. He said the company is trying, but has no plan yet for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to find one.Coxon's argument is partly about candour. Executives soften their phrasing for the press, he wrote, then say the same things privately, and the belief that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade is not a marketing stunt. He also described something that used to be a thought experiment. Models now know when they are being tested, and reason about the fact while it is happening.He pointed to the recent run of cyber incidents at frontier labs, including July's Hugging Face breach, as evidence the risk has left the theoretical stage. Coxon is among more than 1,000 researchers who recently signed a statement calling for governments to coordinate on a way to slow AI development if models start improving on their own. Anthropic has not commented on his departure.
Article Summary: Jacob coxon quit anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested. He said he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation. Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest ipos ever, and safety is the sales pitch.

Article Title: Google unveils five new sustainability initiatives in India
Article Text: Google is expanding its Solar API to cover more than 300 million rooftops in India, enabling faster and more accurate rooftop solar assessments. Installers can now evaluate a home’s solar potential without an on‑site visit, reducing time and cost. Platforms like Solar Ladder and OpenSolar have already integrated Solar API insights to streamline proposal creation and automate manual roof surveys.Google has signed a long‑term agreement with ReNew Power for a 150‑megawatt solar project in Rajasthan. The company will receive environmental attributes from the clean electricity generated, helping address electricity‑related emissions across its value chain. This marks Google’s second Scope 3‑focused solar project in India, bringing total added capacity to 300 MW.Google is partnering with Mitti Labs to help tens of thousands of smallholder rice farmers adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), a climate‑smart farming method that reduces methane emissions and conserves water. The initiative is expected to generate up to 3 million tonnes of CO₂e in near‑term warming impact (GWP20) and conserve billions of gallons of water.NASA‑enabled satellite verification will support monitoring and farmer adoption.The Google Center for Climate Technology has selected three inaugural projects focused on green workforce training and low‑carbon construction materials. Google is adding two new focus areas—water stewardship and waste & circularity—and is inviting proposals via the Manthan Platform. Selected applicants will receive support to develop scalable, data‑driven environmental solutions.Google has welcomed the first cohort of the DeepMind Accelerator: AI for the Planet, featuring four Indian startups: Terrastack, Varaha Climate, Farmers for Forests, and Climitra Carbon. These companies use AI, Geo‑AI, drones and satellite models to empower farmers, scale agroforestry, restore biodiversity, and convert biomass into biochar.These five initiatives reflect Google’s push to combine AI, research partnerships and local innovation to advance sustainable development and climate resilience across India.
Article Summary: Google is expanding its solar api to cover more than 300 million rooftops in india. Google has signed a long‑term agreement with renew power for a 150‑megawatt solar project in rajasthan. Google is partnering with mitti labs to help tens of thousands of smallholder rice farmers adopt alternate wetting and drying (awd)
